s: lame (limited in movement due to injury, defect or paralysis to legs, wings, etc.; especially of animals and their limbs)
weak, tired (exhausted from strain; of limbs, etc.): lame, weak, unconvincing (of excuses, words of protest or defense, etc.)
weak, tired (exhausted from strain; of limbs, etc.): slow (annoyingly so)
lahm.et: From Middle High German lam, from Old High German lam, from Proto-West Germanic *lam, from Proto-Germanic *lamaz.

s: to feel as if one is paralyzed, unable to move or act
This poison paralyzes the breathing muscles.
lähmen.et: From Middle High German lemen, lemmen, from Old High German lemmen, from Proto-Germanic *lamjaną, derived from *lamaz (“lame”), whence German lahm (“lame”). The simplification of the geminate and subsequent lengthening of the vowel by analogy with this underly…

s: lahmacun (Oriental dish consisting of dough topped with meat; a common snack in Germany, often rolled and filled with salad)

Lahm.et: From the adjective lahm (“lame”). Compare the surname Lame.

s: Lahn (a right tributary of the Rhine, Germany)
groyne, breakwater (structure built perpendicular to the shore to prevent erosion)
Lahnung.et: Borrowed from Low German, from Middle Low German lāne (“alley”). Cognates include English lane.

s: a rural district of Hesse; seat: Wetzlar
Lahn-Dill-Kreis.et: From the rivers Lahn and Dill.
